findings.title: Start-headed passages outside the seven members are left to the catch-all row and to task 4.1's discretion
findings.recommendation: Running the requirement's own residual grep over today's README.md and docs/ ("start", "begin", "first change", "new work", "entry", "create") hits three passages that read as where a change starts and that the table settles only through its catch-all row "every other passage: commands named as reference or example": docs/commands.md:38 `## Starting a change` (its first start command is `/orbit:explore`; `/orbit:architect` sits under `## Across the project`), docs/workflows.md:35 `### Step by step` ("create the change with `/orbit:new`", line 37) and docs/workflows.md:140 `### Start a new change when`. D-dr-5's reasoning (a reference order is not a suggestion) is given for the Quick reference and README's command table only; a section HEADED "Starting a change" is not obviously reference. Task 4.1 runs the grep at apply and lets the implementer either add a member or "record why it is not one", so two implementers can ship different lists and different requirement tables. Decide each of the three now, in the requirement's table.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: List `docs/commands.md` › `## Starting a change` as a member (and move or mention `/orbit:architect` at its head, with a task under 2.x); add explicit not-listed rows for workflows.md's `### Step by step` and `### Start a new change when` with their reasons.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Keep the seven members and add an explicit not-listed row naming all three passages, each with its reason (a per-command reference section; an alternative to propose, not where new work starts; a judgement about scope that names no command), so task 4.1 finds them already classified.

findings.title: The walks start at architect but never return to it: no task carries the ratify step the onboard model ends with
findings.recommendation: design.md:7-8 names the shipped onboard body as the model the docs follow: "architect is where new work starts and where it returns", and the onboard flow diagram ends `archive ─→ architect (ratify the stage)` (.claude/skills/orbit-onboard/SKILL.md:65-69). Tasks 2.1 and 2.2 add only the opening architect step. After apply, docs/getting-started.md's walk opens a program at step 0 and ends at `### 7. Archive` (lines 103-111), leaving the reader's stage archived-but-unratified with no word on the closing session; the archive emit's `next_recommended` now names `/orbit:architect <doc>` (orbit-architect's strict row), so the reader meets a next step the page never mentions. README's numbered list (task 2.1) has the same gap. Either add the closing step or state the omission as a decision.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Extend tasks 2.1 and 2.2: getting-started gains a closing step after Archive (`/orbit:architect <program>` reviews and ratifies the stage), and README's list ends with the same line.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Record in design.md's Decisions that the walks open at architect but leave ratification to the commands page, and say so in one sentence at the end of getting-started's Archive step.

findings.title: getting-started's intro counts "the six commands of a first change", which task 2.1 makes seven
findings.recommendation: docs/getting-started.md:3-4 says the README Quickstart "lists the six commands of a first change". README's `### Your first change` list has six entries today (README.md:100-106); task 2.1 opens it with `/orbit:architect <program>`, making seven, and no task touches getting-started's intro, so the page states a wrong count after apply (no check reads it). Add to task 2.2 (or 2.1): update getting-started's intro count, or drop the number.

findings.title: The fenced `<id> ──►` form does not say the id is a whole word
findings.recommendation: "inside a fence, `<id>` followed by ` ──►`" leaves word boundaries open: `ff` is a suffix of `diff`, `new` of `renew`, so a fence drawing `diff ──►` would read as an `ff` start under a substring matcher and not under a word matcher. No listed fence draws such a word today (the members' fences draw explore, propose, review, apply, archive, specs, tasks, design), so this is a precision gap, not a live failure. Say "`<id>` as a whole word (not preceded by a letter, digit or hyphen) followed by ` ──►`".

findings.title: Starting the workflow-engine diagram at architect sits against its section's "each workflow is an action on [a change]"
findings.recommendation: docs/workflow-engine.md:14-15 says "A change is a folder of artifacts, and each workflow is an action on it", and the diagram's return loop (lines 17-21) means "edit any artifact, at any point". An architect session acts on an architecture doc, not on a change, and task 2.4 asks for architect at the diagram's head "without changing what the section says about actions on a change". Name the form in the task, e.g. `architect ──► explore ──► …` with the loop still spanning propose…archive only, and one clause saying architect plans the program before the change exists.

findings.title: concepts `## Artifacts`' new architect sentence has no owner on its Carried by line
findings.recommendation: Task 2.5 adds a sentence placing explore after architect to docs/concepts.md's `## Artifacts`, and says "keep its Carried by: line valid". The line today (docs/concepts.md:104) names the 1.3.1 baseline, `orbit-explore-modifications` and `orbit-propose-modifications`; the carried-by check passes whether or not the new claim's owner is named, so "valid" is met trivially. The new sentence's owner is `orbit-architect` (its `Start surfaces name the architect workflow first`). State in the task that `orbit-architect` joins the line.

stale_suppressed.title: Task 1.4 expects all seven sections to fail while design.md says the probe found six of seven leading with explore
stale_suppressed.evidence: design.md:38-41's "six of the seven" counted the earlier `## Changes` member; the listed `## Artifacts` (docs/concepts.md:83-104) names `/orbit:explore` at line 98 and its fence draws `proposal ──►` (not a start id), so all seven listed sections lead with explore today: README.md:100, getting-started.md:18, workflows.md:21, workflows.md:51, workflows.md:177, workflow-engine.md:17 (fence `explore ──►`), concepts.md:98.

commentary: The check itself is well specified: section bounds, the two match forms, the missing-heading failure and the order-not-absence reading are each stated once and line up with tasks 1.1-1.4. I ran the listed members against today's pages (all seven lead with explore, so 1.4's red run is reachable), validated the change strict, confirmed the MODIFIED blocks carry every baseline scenario, and ran the requirement's residual grep myself. The pattern behind the findings is that the change specifies its OPENING edits precisely and leaves the edges to apply-time judgement: which start-headed passages are not start sections, whether the walks return to architect, and the sentences around each edit that the new step makes stale. All are doc-scope and cheap to settle in the artifacts now; none touches engine behaviour. Readings from the live checkout (HEAD 00d6289a).

direction.reasoning:
The change is small, its instrument is precise, and its premise is measured: the seven listed sections lead with explore today and the check will see them flip.
The open points are classification and completeness calls at the edges of the docs edit, settled by a short walk in the artifacts; none needs a redesign or a different scope.
